reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as a TechBoomers tutorial on navigating AliExpress customer service and using its chat box to ask questions. The references to related articles, tutorials, subscriptions, and site visits are described as ordinary educational cross-promotion rather than conditions for a deceptive offer.

citations.quote: In this video, i'll show you how to contact AliExpress Customer Service.
First open your web browser and go to aliexpress com, and at the top of the page, click Help. Then, click Customer Service.
If that doesn't solve your problem, you can talk to an Aliexpress customer service representative.
Scroll to the bottom of the page and click CHAT NOW.

opening.argument: The video links viewer actions to a concrete benefit: visiting TechBoomers.com is presented as the route to access “over 100 free courses.” That is a low-barrier acquisition funnel, reinforced by the instruction to click through to the site and by the separate subscription prompt shown at the end. The AliExpress tutorial supplies the attention and credibility, while the requested click and subscription create the participation pathway. The content therefore functions as a solicitation attached to an easy-to-obtain educational reward, rather than as a purely neutral demonstration.

citations.quote: Visit http://www.techboomers.com for over 100 free courses on all of today's most popular websites & apps!
If you're interested in trying some alternatives to AliExpress, check out our Sites Like AliExpress article on TechBoomers.com.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the links ordinary cross-promotion does not answer the action-benefit linkage. The description explicitly pairs visiting the external site with access to more than 100 free courses, and the end screen explicitly asks viewers to subscribe and go to TechBoomers.com. The tutorial framing makes those calls to action more credible, but does not make them non-solicitational.

citations.quote: Visit http://www.techboomers.com for over 100 free courses on all of today's most popular websites & apps!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted material shows only that TechBoomers advertises free educational material and asks viewers to visit or subscribe. It does not show a cash payment, asset, withdrawal, generator, verification flow, or deceptive promise. A free course is an educational resource, and the AliExpress instructions remain the video's central subject; promotional calls alone do not establish a scam.

citations.quote: Watch this short tutorial video to learn how to contact AliExpress customer service.
In this video, i'll show you how to contact AliExpress Customer Service.

opening.argument: Several solicitation signals appear together: an external website is promoted, viewers are asked to subscribe, and the destination is associated with a large quantity of free courses. The end screen gives direct click-oriented instructions rather than merely naming a resource, while the narration adds another TechBoomers destination through its alternatives article. This combination can steer viewers from a practical support question into an external acquisition funnel whose promised benefit is easy access to free material. The unusually low barrier and repeated calls to action are the relevant warning signs.

citations.quote: Visit http://www.techboomers.com for over 100 free courses on all of today's most popular websites & apps!
If you're interested in trying some alternatives to AliExpress, check out our Sites Like AliExpress article on TechBoomers.com.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on the tutorial steps but leaves the promotional pattern unaddressed. The video ends with direct prompts to subscribe and visit an external site, while the description advertises over 100 free courses. Those signals matter because the viewer arrives for customer-service help and is then redirected toward a broad external offering.

citations.quote: Visit http://www.techboomers.com for over 100 free courses on all of today's most popular websites & apps!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The alleged red flags are not scam-specific. The material contains no return, income, investment, payment, crypto, gift-card, or account-verification claim. The visible end screen asks for a subscription and site visit, but it does not promise money or an asset; the description identifies the destination as free courses, and the spoken content explains customer-service navigation.

citations.quote: First open your web browser and go to aliexpress com, and at the top of the page, click Help. Then, click Customer Service.
Do you learn better by reading? A text version is available at: https://techboomers.com/t/contact-aliexpress-customer-service

opening.argument: Although packaged as instruction, the video also operates as promotion for TechBoomers. The branded tutorial directs viewers to a related article, advertises a large library of free courses, and ends with explicit prompts to subscribe and visit the website. The AliExpress procedure supplies useful context, but it also creates a trusted route into the promoter's broader content ecosystem. This is therefore not merely neutral education: it steers participation toward an externally controlled site in exchange for access to its low-cost educational offering.

citations.quote: Visit http://www.techboomers.com for over 100 free courses on all of today's most popular websites & apps!
If you're interested in trying some alternatives to AliExpress, check out our Sites Like AliExpress article on TechBoomers.com.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the tutorial label as dispositive, but the video's own closing material broadens the objective beyond AliExpress support. It promotes a related article, a large course library, subscription, and a site visit. That is a participation funnel embedded in educational framing, so calling it ordinary instruction does not resolve the promotional steering.

citations.quote: If you're interested in trying some alternatives to AliExpress, check out our Sites Like AliExpress article on TechBoomers.com.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion does not equal a scam. The video openly identifies itself as a tutorial and describes the external material as a text version and free courses. Nothing quoted promises money, a digital asset, or a withdrawal in exchange for clicking. The AliExpress navigation and chat instructions are concrete educational content, not evidence of a deceptive acquisition scheme.
